seasonal_signs: Afternoon sea breezes arrive from the south-west
animals: Young birds begin venturing out of their nests
traditional_practices: Controlled burning of Country was traditionally carried out during Birak
During this season, Noongar people would move towards coastal areas

seasonal_signs: There is little to no rain
Hot easterly wind in the morning and cool sea breezes in the afternoon
animals: Dolphins and calves close to shore
food: Fish such as tailor, mullet and marron
traditional_practices: Traditionally a time for living and fishing around the coast, rivers and estuaries

seasonal_signs: Hot weather begins to ease and nights become cooler
Light breezes generally arrive from southerly directions
Conditions become wetter and damper as the season progresses
animals: Flying ants become quite common and can often be seen in the air
traditional_practices: Mia mias (traditional shelters) were repaired and prepared for the wetter winter months

seasonal_signs: Coldest and wettest time of the year
Waterways and water bodies begin to fill
Cold westerly and southerly winds become much more common
animals: Many animals begin pairing up in preparation for breeding
Black swans (Mali) start to gather around lakes and rivers as they start to prepare for nesting and breeding
food: Food sources shift from the sea, estuaries and lakes towards land-based animals
traditional_practices: Traditionally a time for Noongar people to live and fish around the coast, rivers and estuaries
Kangaroo skins were used to make bookas (animal-skin cloaks) for the colder weather

seasonal_signs: The days get warmer but they are mixed with rainy and windy conditions
A major flowering period begins across the South West
animals: Djilba is a major season for animal births
Koolbardi (magpies), Djidi djidi (willy wagtails) and chuck-a-luck (wattlebirds) protect their young
traditional_practices: Noongar children were traditionally taught the different wildlife, foraging and respecting protective animals
As rain decreased and temperatures increased, families would begin to move from their inland camps towards coastal areas

seasonal_signs: Rain begins to ease and days start to become drier
Coastal cold fronts become less frequent
animals: Snakes and other reptiles come out of hibernation as temperatures rise
traditional_practices: Families would begin to move from their inland camps towards coastal areas
